title: Fuselage — Fwd Cargo Door Surround — Detailed Inspection of the Corner Fittings

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: A detailed visual and eddy current inspection of the four corner fittings of the forward cargo door cut-out, repeated every 3 000 flight cycles from a threshold of 22 000 flight cycles.

sections.planning_reason: Re-substantiation of the forward cargo door surround against the high-density freight loading spectrum showed a reserve factor shortfall at the four lower corner fittings. The crack growth curve for the aluminium-lithium fitting predicts initiation between 34 000 and 42 000 flight cycles and gives a detectable crack length at about 22 000 cycles. Operators of combi and heavy-cargo aircraft therefore need a repeat inspection well before the fleet leader reaches the initiation band. This Service Bulletin puts that inspection in place while the structural solution is developed.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives a detailed visual inspection of the four corner fittings of the forward cargo door cut-out and an eddy current inspection of the frame web at station C40 in the fastener rows adjacent to each fitting. The inspection is done once at the threshold and then repeated at the interval given in the compliance time. It does not change the aircraft standard and no part is replaced. Findings inside the limits given in the accomplishment instructions are recorded and the aircraft is returned to service; findings outside those limits are reported to Aeralis for disposition.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the forward cargo compartment and remove the lower shell lining panels in zones 113 and 115. Do the removal steps of task AMM-M-53-21-13-000-001-A as far as the point at which the fitting flange is visible, but do not remove the fittings. Clean the fitting flanges and the adjacent web surface. Do a detailed visual inspection of each of the four fittings, with particular attention to the load introduction radius. Do an eddy current inspection of the frame web assembly D5321003375416 in the two fastener rows on each side of every fitting. Record every indication with its position relative to the frame station and the stringer. Report any indication longer than 8 mm to Aeralis before further work. Install the lining panels and do the door operational test.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft. The threshold and the repeat interval are counted from aircraft delivery and are the same for every aircraft in the effectivity.
sections.material_note: No kit and no consumable parts other than cleaning agent and the standard protective treatment restoration set. An eddy current probe suitable for 2 MHz operation and the surface reference block for aluminium-lithium are needed and are not supplied with this Service Bulletin.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the accumulation of 22 000 flight cycles since new, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 3 000 flight cycles.

title: Fuselage — Fwd Cargo Door Surround — One-Off Detailed Inspection of the Corner Fittings

issue.reason: Effectivity restricted to pre-modification aircraft, the repeat inspection withdrawn and the remaining accomplishment restated as the one-off baseline record taken before the titanium fitting standard is embodied.

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: A one-off detailed visual and eddy current inspection of the four corner fittings of the forward cargo door cut-out, to find and record any pre-existing indication before the titanium fitting standard is embodied.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft delivered before the production cut-in of the titanium corner fitting standard carry aluminium-lithium fittings that do not meet the revised high-density freight loading spectrum. The fatigue substantiation predicts crack initiation between 34 000 and 42 000 flight cycles against a design service goal well above that. The repeat interval published at the first issue was derived from the crack growth curve of the aluminium-lithium fitting and has no meaning once the titanium standard is installed, because the flange stiffness and the residual stress state after machining are both different. Before the fittings are replaced, operators also need a recorded baseline of the frame web condition, because a crack that has already started in the web will not be removed by changing the fitting and must be dispositioned separately.
sections.description: This issue withdraws the repeat inspection and keeps a single one-off accomplishment, which is now the baseline record taken before the corner fittings are replaced. The inspection content is unchanged: a detailed visual inspection of the four corner fittings and an eddy current inspection of the frame web at station C40. It does not change the aircraft standard. Aircraft already brought to the titanium standard of MOD-160142 are outside the effectivity of this Service Bulletin; the surveillance of the titanium fitting is set by the operator maintenance programme and not by a repeat interval published here.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the forward cargo compartment and remove the lower shell lining panels in zones 113 and 115. Do the removal steps of task AMM-M-53-21-13-000-001-A as far as the point at which the fitting flange is visible, but do not remove the fittings. Clean the fitting flanges and the adjacent web surface. Do a detailed visual inspection of each of the four fittings, with particular attention to the load introduction radius. Do an eddy current inspection of the frame web assembly D5321003375416 in the two fastener rows on each side of every fitting. Record every indication with its position relative to the frame station and the stringer. Report any indication longer than 8 mm to Aeralis before further work. Install the lining panels and do the door operational test.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00300 that have not yet been brought to the titanium corner fitting standard of MOD-160142. Aircraft delivered from MSN M00300 onward are already at that standard and are not affected, and an aircraft that has embodied Service Bulletin MRD-53-1012 is released from this Service Bulletin on the date of embodiment.
sections.material_note: No kit and no consumable parts other than cleaning agent and the standard protective treatment restoration set. An eddy current probe suitable for 2 MHz operation and the surface reference block for aluminium-lithium are needed and are not supplied with this Service Bulletin.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the accomplishment of Service Bulletin MRD-53-1012, and in any case within 36 months after the date of this revision. The 3 000 flight cycle repeat interval published at revision 01 is withdrawn.

revision_history.reason: Effectivity limited to pre MOD-160142 aircraft, repeat interval withdrawn
